source.version: Part 14 — Abiotic Disorders and Diagnostic Reasoning — Batch 02
source.publicationAuthorization: Project owner authorized continued website publication on 2026-08-29. Independent specialist approval remains a separate project-control field and is not implied by publication.
source.releaseTimeReview: THC-ENC-266–270 were reconciled against the controlled Volume 14 manuscript plus plant-water-relations and hypoxia mechanisms, greenhouse oedema physiology with explicit cross-species limits, cannabis temperature-response evidence, and controlled cannabis high-light studies. Public wording separates dry-media water shortage from wet-media uptake failure, treats oedema as a physiological water-imbalance differential rather than infection, rejects universal heat/cold injury temperatures, and rejects a universal PPFD threshold for high-light injury.
source.note: This batch publishes wet-versus-dry wilt, oedema, heat stress, cold/chilling stress, and high-light/photoinhibition injury.
